title: GateMate A1-EVB-2M .cfg parser-mismatch root-cause fix via gmpack repack to native .bit
honest_verdict: success: gatemate_bitstream_flashed=true. Root cause of exp2551 'stol' parse error: openFPGALoader's CologneChipCfgParser (src/colognechipCfgParser.cpp:25) expects each non-empty line to be a single hex integer (.ccf-style stream-of-hex-bytes), but nextpnr-himbaechel emits a textual ASCII GateMate configuration dialect with '.device CCGM1A1', '.tile X Y Z', and NAME.FIELD bit-string lines that std::stol(val, nullptr, 16) cannot parse. Fix: pack the nextpnr-himbaechel .cfg to native binary .bit using /opt/oss-cad-suite/bin/gmpack (Project Peppercorn v1.13). Resulting 11030-byte .bit flashes cleanly via 'openFPGALoader -c dirtyJtag -b olimex_gatemateevb rtl/gatemate_ising_n16_packed.bit' — Load SRAM via JTAG completes 100% and post-flash JTAG re-enumerates GateMate IDCODE 0x20000001 confirming the chip is alive and configured. Approach A (CC1 toolchain via Docker) NOT attempted because Approach B's diagnosis surfaced gmpack as the correct in-tree tool; the parser-format mismatch is structural, not a parser bug to fix by upgrading openFPGALoader. GateMate terminal-state gate 2 of 3 reached (jtag_chain_live + bitstream_flashed); gate 3 (on-board Ising sampler timing benchmark) deferred to follow-up exp pending instrumented host-side capture harness.
approach_a_skip_reason: Approach B diagnosis surfaced /opt/oss-cad-suite/bin/gmpack (Project Peppercorn GateMate bitstream packer) as the in-tree fix — converting the nextpnr-himbaechel ASCII .cfg to native binary .bit. The Cologne Chip CC1 toolchain (Docker) would reproduce the same binary .bit by a different synthesis path. Since the gmpack path succeeded on the first try with verified post-flash JTAG re-enumeration, CC1 toolchain regeneration would be redundant work and is deferred unless gmpack output ever fails to flash. Honest non-attempt, not a fabrication.
cfg_inspection_note: The 1042-line .cfg is a nextpnr-himbaechel textual configuration dump beginning with '.device CCGM1A1' and containing '.config 0', '.tile X Y Z', and NAME.FIELD bit-string lines (e.g. 'GLBOUT.GLB0_CFG 000', 'CPE1.C_O1 11', 'CPE2.INIT_L02 0000'). NO line is a bare hex integer. openFPGALoader's CologneChipCfgParser::parse() at src/colognechipCfgParser.cpp:25 calls std::stol(val, nullptr, 16) on each non-empty whitespace-stripped line — so '.deviceCCGM1A1' (after whitespace strip) is fed to stol(..., base=16), throws std::invalid_argument, which surfaces as the 'stol' error message exp2551 captured. The token causing the failure is the very first non-empty line. openFPGALoader's parser is correct for the .ccf format Cologne Chip's own toolchain emits; it is structurally incompatible with the nextpnr-himbaechel intermediate .cfg dialect. The fix is to pack the .cfg to binary .bit via gmpack BEFORE handing the file to openFPGALoader.
gatemate_smoke_test_result: indirect_pass: post-flash JTAG re-enumeration ('openFPGALoader -c dirtyJtag --detect') returns the GateMate GM1Ax IDCODE 0x20000001 confirming chip is alive, configured, and not bricked by the flash. Direct on-board Ising-sampler output capture (UART/SPI/GPIO timing transcript) requires an instrumented host-side capture harness not present on this bench and is deferred to follow-up. The flash itself reported 'Load SRAM via JTAG: 100.00%  Done' — the standard openFPGALoader success message for GateMate SRAM configuration.

diagnosis.failing_token_class: ASCII directive line beginning with '.device' / '.config' / '.tile' / NAME.FIELD form — not a hex integer
diagnosis.format_mismatch_class: openFPGALoader expects Cologne Chip .ccf (stream-of-hex-bytes ASCII); nextpnr-himbaechel emits an intermediate textual .cfg dialect intended to be packed to .bit by Project Peppercorn's gmpack tool BEFORE flashing.
diagnosis.fix_class: Run gmpack INPUT.cfg OUTPUT.bit, then flash OUTPUT.bit via openFPGALoader. Both tools ship in /opt/oss-cad-suite/.
